- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh: lines 1774-1776 (comment-building block) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The comment-building block references `${RB_SECURITY_ORIGINAL_ACTION}`, `${RB_SECURITY_BLOCKING_COUNT}`, and `${RB_SECURITY_BLOCKING_ISSUES}` without `:-` defaults.
  WHY: The extracted test runs the block under `set -euo pipefail` without initializing those variables, so the unbound-variable reference aborts the script and fails CI.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh: line 2164 (`rb_security_disable_auto_merge` call in the fix-push block) and the function body in `scripts/review_rb_judge_security_pass.sh:218-233` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `rb_security_disable_auto_merge` returns the exit code of its final head-match check, so it returns 1 when the live PR head moved even though auto-merge withdrawal succeeded.
  WHY: The caller exits the judge run, leaving auto-merge disabled but no judge decision posted; a subsequent review run can re-enter the same path.
- scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh: lines 176-190 (shallow-checkout ancestor re-check in `single_pass_extensions`) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The unshallow fetch has no timeout.
  WHY: A slow fetch on a long-lived integration branch can delay the synchronous judge step without a timeout.
- Requirement: "The judge may: `merge` or `merge_with_followup`, with open findings of any severity. The findings stay open as issues. `implement.yml` resolves their `Integration branch:` through `retarget_merged_base.sh`, so they are fixed against the default branch once this PR merges." (PR description, "An exhausted security pass goes to the judge instead of a human" section, first bullet.)
  Expected change site: `scripts/review_rb_judge_security_pass.sh::rb_security_severity_block` and the `case` in `scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1751-1765` that consumes its verdict.
  Evidence of absence: `rb_security_severity_block` (helpers file:93-110) classifies every severity other than `low`/`medium` as `blocking`, then the judge `case` converts a `merge`/`merge_with_followup` action to `fix` (or `hold` on the final round) whenever `RB_SECURITY_BLOCKING_COUNT` is > 0. The accompanying changelog fragment `changelog.d/6400-rb-judge-security-severity-block.md` (also added in this PR) explicitly contradicts the PR description and states the opposite behavior is shipped: "The review-blocked judge no longer merges single-issue PRs with unresolved high, critical, or unrated security findings after audit exhaustion. It fixes and re-audits while retries remain, then holds the PR for a clean audit or a human decision." The code follows the changelog, so the PR description and the shipped behavior disagree about whether a `merge` verdict with blocking findings is reachable from the exhaustion judge. Either the PR description or the changelog is wrong, and a reader of the PR will form the wrong mental model of the shipped behavior.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
